page: Amazon Web Services m5.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance split between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall consistently in the average range. This includes stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth read-only small block cached operations reach 1507.0 GB/sec, while uncached large block reads and writes perform at 108.25 GB/sec and 47.62 GB/sec respectively.

Given the average multi-core capabilities and weak single-core performance, the m5.8xlarge is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads rather than single-threaded compute-heavy tasks. It handles static web serving, Redis SET operations, and software compilation with average efficiency. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model scoring in the bottom 10% at 3.88 tokens/sec. The instance is best deployed for balanced workloads such as web serving, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
